minutes.headline: Finance Committee split up board liaison seats by roll call vote after hearing of a FY22 state-aid deficit.
minutes.summary: The town manager reported a deficit after the state budget and cherry sheet, tied partly to school choice estimates, and described how ARPA funds might be used. The committee then divided its liaison and committee assignments by roll call vote, leaving several open. It began discussing whether to comment on the 40B project to MassHousing, and the captions end before that was settled.

budget_items.topic: FY22 state budget and cherry sheet deficit
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager said the governor signed the state budget and the cherry sheet leaves the town with a deficit. New growth may offset it, and a fall special town meeting is planned for adjustments.
Staff said the governor's budget used an estimate rather than actual FY21 spending, so the rise looks large against the estimate but small against what was actually paid.
The town learned the state budget included an earmark for LED lighting at the library.

budget_items.topic: Pay as you throw bag price
budget_items.what_was_said: The select board raised bag costs, and a senior relief program was considered but not adopted.
The veterans agent resigned and the stipended position is being recruited.
The town manager discussed possible eligible uses and said funds must be used by fiscal 23. She wants projects that add no burden to the town or its staff.
A member said the pro forma underestimates infrastructure costs. Another thought the school impact estimate was understated, and the chair mentioned a consultant grant that comes with such projects.

decisions.decision: Assignments agreed: green communities tabled until its committee is established; the cemetery commission/DPW liaison left unassigned until the absent member is present; the planning board liaison left open.
Chair will post for the 40B workshop in case a quorum attends, though the select board will post it.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee approved its slate of committee and liaison assignments by unanimous roll call vote.
Three assignments were left open: green communities (tabled until its committee exists), the cemetery commission/DPW liaison, and the planning board liaison.
The town manager said the governor signed the state budget and the cherry sheet leaves the town with a FY22 deficit, which new growth may offset.
A fall special town meeting is planned for adjustments, and ARPA funds must be used by fiscal 23.
The committee began discussing a comment to MassHousing on the 40B project; the captions end without a resolution.

why_it_matters: A state-aid shortfall in FY22 can mean the town covers the gap from new growth or through changes voted at a fall special town meeting, which residents may be asked to approve.
The 40B project's infrastructure and school costs were questioned by members, and the committee's comment to MassHousing, if sent, would bear on how those costs are weighed.
watch_next: A fall special town meeting for FY22 budget adjustments, as the town manager described.
Whether the committee sends a comment on the 40B project to MassHousing; the captions do not show a decision.
